newsitem.title: UK: Brady market rangebound ahead of FOMC next week.
newsitem.headline: Brady market rangebound ahead of FOMC next week.

text.p: Brady bond prices were mixed in extremely light trade on Friday as players kept to the sidelines ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting July 1-2 and a slew of U.S. economic reports due later today and through next week, traders said.
"The reason London is so quiet is because a lot of people are looking ahead to the FOMC and the heavy calendar next week," said one emerging market trader at a major U.S. bank.
Even though few expect the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates next week, traders said the market is unlikely to make any bold moves until the rate uncertainty is removed.

Key economic reports which the Brady market will focus on include U.S. gross domestic product (GDP) at 1230 GMT today, the June National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) on Tuesday and the U.S. jobs report on Thursday.
One Brady bond trader suggested any market weakness could prompt some buying heading into next week. "There could be some buying on softness," the trader said.
Among Eastern European Brady instruments, Bulgarian prices were mostly unchanged as expectations for the implementation of the currency board on July 1 have already been discounted.
Russian Vneshekonombank dollar loans, which rose briefly on shortcovering by local buyers, were also unchanged at 90-3/4 bid.
In the Latin Brady market, Mexican debt was unchanged to mildly weaker ahead of the country's Congressional elections next week.
Mexican par bonds were unchanged at 77-1/8 and
the country's discount bonds were 1/4 lower at 92-3/4 bid.
